Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: There is no explicit marker for the absolutive case.
curated_comment: Amam (amam1246, Trans-New Guinea, Papua New Guinea) shows tense/aspect-conditioned split ergativity documented in Aki and Pennington (2013). Ergative-absolutive alignment occurs in past/perfective and future/irrealis contexts; nominative-accusative alignment in present/imperfective (GB409_6=0). Additionally, a topicality split: when A is topical, the ergative marker is absent (GB409_16=0). Ergative absent in subordinate clauses (GB409_21=0). All 24 features verified against Aki and Pennington (2013). Glottocode amam1246 is correct.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: First-person pronouns show ergative-absolutive alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: Second-person pronouns show ergative-absolutive alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: Third-person pronouns show ergative-absolutive alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs exhibit ergative-absolutive alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: NOM-ACC alignment occurs in imperfective/present tense clauses (tense/aspect-conditioned split).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Ergative-absolutive alignment occurs in perfective aspect clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: Ergative-absolutive alignment in past tense clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: Future tense aligns with past/perfective using the ergative system; present uses NOM-ACC.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: Ergative alignment in the indicative mood, conditioned by tense/aspect.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: Ergative alignment attested in interrogative mood; imperative lacks ergative marking.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: Ergative alignment in realis status, conditioned by tense/aspect.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Ergative-absolutive alignment in irrealis (future/hypothetical) status.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: Ergative alignment applies to agentive A arguments.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Ergative alignment applies to some non-agentive A arguments.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: The ergative marker is obligatorily absent when A is topical (topic-drop/antipassive-like pattern).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: Ergative marking is mandatory when A is non-topical/focused.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Ergative alignment applies to animate A arguments.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: Ergative-absolutive alignment applies to inanimate A arguments.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Ergative-absolutive alignment occurs in main clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Ergative-absolutive alignment is absent in subordinate clauses.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Ergative alignment is conditioned by pragmatic factors: topicality and subject focus determine marker presence.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Ergative and genitive markers are distinct morphemes.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Ergative and instrumental/comitative markers are distinct morphemes.
